Undated rows take the date of the nearest dated row above them (DESIGN 3.4). `primary` has the usual epoch `set` and `team` rows at the top (nothing dated above them, so they stay undated and apply from the beginning) and a dated `set anchor` at 2026-06-01T09:00. Three undated rows sit mid-tab as typed: a `team` row adding dave under the shift of 8 June, and under the shift of 15 June a `set tolerance=1` row followed by a chained `set seed=3` row. On read they inherit 2026-06-08T09:00 and 2026-06-15T09:00 respectively, sort at those instants before the shift by type order (the `team` row therefore applies to bob's 8 June shift, so dave is on the roster from then at the roster minimum, and the two `set` rows keep their document order), and are written back dated: `expected/primary.csv` shows the materialised starts, so a second run reads ordinary dated rows and changes nothing. In `#Global` the undated `set seed=9` row under the dated `set precredit=0` row inherits 2026-06-01T09:00 (`expected/global.csv`). `now` is 2026-06-29T10:00 with no stored snapshot: the four pinned history shifts are kept, the snapshot lands at 06-29 with everyone on 7, and the round robin continues alice, bob, carol, dave; `expected/status.txt` shows `tolerance 1` and `seed 3` from the rotation layer, which hides the global `seed 9`, and `precredit 0` from the global layer.
